descriptor: Producing copper miner (MATSA, Spain & Motheo, Botswana) · FY ends 30 June · reported in USD from FY2022 · quoted in AUD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the FY2026 EBITDA margin (52.5%) is a cyclical peak from an elevated copper price and favourable TC/RC terms, not a sustainable level -- the DCF fades margin toward a ~40% mid-cycle floor. Read this chart as "how far above mid-cycle are we now", not a trend to extrapolate.

What to watch:

  • Margin reverting toward mid-cycle as the copper price and TC/RC normalise
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital, cash taxes)
  • MATSA vs Motheo unit operating costs (A$/t processed) disclosed in the filings, which the CSV does not capture

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is copper (and by-product gold/silver/zinc) concentrate sales from MATSA (Spain) and Motheo (Botswana), driven by tonnes shipped, ore grade, and the realised copper price net of treatment/refining charges (TC/RC).

For Sandfire Resources Limited: FY2026 revenue of US$1.65bn is a record set at the confluence of an elevated copper price and an unusually favourable TC/RC environment, not a steady-state run-rate -- Motheo only reached first production in Feb-2023, so most of the reported history is a ramp-up, not maturity.

What to watch:

  • Revenue swings driven by the copper price, not volume growth
  • Motheo's production ramp versus MATSA's more mature output
  • Interim rows show H1/H2 seasonality in shipments

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Sandfire Resources Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (mid-cycle fade, not FY2026's record margin)
